title: Linear inequalities
examples: When do I have to flip the inequality sign?
How do I show the answer on the number line?
Can I solve an inequality with fractions?

explain.say: Today we are learning about linear inequalities. These are like equations but use signs like less than or greater than.
First, we must remember the rule for multiplying or dividing by a negative number. If you flip the sign, you must also flip the inequality sign.
For example, if we have negative two times x is greater than negative six. We divide by negative two, so we flip the sign.
Next, we show the solution on a number line. We use a circle with an open dot if the sign is strictly less than or greater than.

items: Use an open circle on number line

explain.say: If the sign includes equals, like less than or equal to, we use a closed dot on the number line. This means the number is included in the answer.

items: Use a closed dot on number line

faq.q: What do I do if I have to divide by a negative number?
faq.a: You must flip the inequality sign you are using. This is a very important rule to remember always. You might also be asked to show this on a number line.
asks: Do I flip the sign when dividing by negative?
What happens to the inequality sign with negative division?

faq.q: How do I show the answer on the number line?
faq.a: You draw a number line and place a dot at the boundary number. An open circle means it is not included, and a closed dot means it is included.
asks: What does the dot on the number line mean?
How do I graph the solution?

faq.q: What does an integer solution mean?
faq.a: It means we are only looking for whole numbers as answers. For example, if the answer is less than five, the integer solutions are four, three, two, and so on.
asks: Are only whole numbers allowed answers?
What are the integer values for this inequality?

faq.q: Can I solve inequalities with variables on both sides?
faq.a: Yes, you can treat it like solving an equation. You move the variable terms to one side and the numbers to the other side.
asks: What if I have x on both sides?
How do I collect the variables?

faq.q: Is it okay to multiply both sides by a negative number?
faq.a: You can multiply both sides, but you absolutely must remember to flip the inequality sign. Forgetting this step will give you the wrong answer.
asks: Must I flip the sign when multiplying by negative?
What is the rule for negative multiplication?

facts: Inequalities use signs like less than (<) or greater than (>).
When multiplying or dividing by a negative number, the inequality sign must be reversed.
A closed dot on a number line means the number is included in the solution.
Integer solutions are the whole numbers that satisfy the inequality.

quiz.say: Which inequality represents all integers greater than or equal to negative two?
quiz.why: Greater than or equal to means we use the 'greater than or equal to' sign, which is represented by a closed dot at negative two.

wrong.0: This uses an open circle, suggesting negative two is not part of the answer.
wrong.1: This represents numbers less than negative two, which is the opposite of what is asked.
wrong.2: This only shows one single number, not all the integers from that point onwards.

quiz.say: If the solution to an inequality is x < 5, what is the largest integer solution?
quiz.why: If x is less than five, the largest whole number that is still smaller than five is four.

wrong.0: The inequality is strictly less than five, so five itself is not included.
wrong.1: Six is larger than five, so it does not satisfy the inequality.
wrong.2: The question specifically asks for the largest integer solution, not a decimal number.
